validated_work_order.understanding:
PR #9 (squash 026f8b6) shipped a user-visible custom-report fix and merged with nothing under upcoming-release-notes/. Verified on main: the commit touches 11 files, none under upcoming-release-notes/; the directory holds 92 entries and none describes this fix. What a person sees is the next Actual release's changelog, which omits it. The contract underneath is the release-note front matter, enforced by packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs — read, not inferred: validateFile() requires a category (after categoryAutocorrections) in categoryOrder, a non-empty authors array of real people (NON_PERSON_AUTHORS = ['claude','github-actions'], plus /\\[bot\\]$/), and a body that is non-empty and free of '\\n'. One markdown file is the whole surface.

CHANGES FROM v1, answering the single rejection. v1 marked all four criteria verify:"test" while declaring no tests[], and its AC-4 how_to_verify plus qa_script step 4 described a shell command no CI job performs — so no criterion was provable and QA was pushed toward citing a "ci" that does not exist. This version keeps verify:"test" (correct: nothing about a markdown file is observable at a live URL, so browser would be a lie too) and makes the proof route honest and explicit on ALL FOUR criteria, not just AC-4: QA runs the repository's own checker inside the PR checkout after the note is committed, saves its stdout under $QA_EVIDENCE_DIR as the evidence for its own case, and cites that case's id — explicitly NOT the literal "ci". A risks[] entry names this as the thing to watch in review, so the mistake is visible rather than latent.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The PR that shipped the fix added no release note, and nothing in this repository's CI fails on a missing one. The composite action .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml runs the checker, but `grep -rln 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns no workflow file — it is referenced by nothing. .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml runs typecheck, lint, unit, build and e2e only; the sole release-notes reference in any workflow is sdlc-release.yml's unrelated publishing job. The requirement in the contributing docs is therefore advisory, and a squashed bot-authored PR slipped past it. The gap is real, but its remedy lives under .github/**, which no plan may change — filed as out_of_scope rather than smuggled into this diff.

`category: Bugfix` is the intended spelling. The issue body and IAC-2 both name it, contributing/index.md:136 lists it as valid, and the checker autocorrects it to Bugfixes before validating. Two existing notes already use the bare form, so it is the local convention, not a typo.

The issue's IAC-3 tail — "that 'Show empty rows' no longer drops the categories that were unchecked" — reads, literally, as the opposite of what shipped: the fix makes unchecked categories stop appearing rather than start appearing. I resolved it in favour of the shipped behaviour, because the issue's own summary sentence ("it fixes 'show empty rows' ignoring unchecked categories"), the commit message ("Unchecked categories rendered as 0.00 rows whenever 'Show empty rows' was on"), and the diff in custom-spreadsheet.ts / grouped-spreadsheet.ts all agree: narrowing the axis removes the phantom rows. AC-3 states that reading explicitly so QA does not re-derive it from the issue's phrasing. If the maintainer meant the literal reading, the note's body is the single line to change.
unknowns: Whether the maintainer prefers the UI label in the note quoted exactly as the sidebar renders it ('Show empty rows', ReportSidebar.tsx:494) or unquoted. I used the exact label, which is the phrasing a reader recognises.

Whether the maintainer prefers the shorter command phrasing chosen here (105 characters) or a longer two-clause form. Prose taste cannot fail the gate; 78 of the 92 existing bodies exceed 80 characters, so the one-line rule is about physical lines, not width.
residual_risks: All four criteria rest on a command no CI job runs, because the repository does not wire the release-notes check into any workflow. QA must run it by hand and cite its own case; that is a documented instruction, not an enforced one. Wiring the check into ci-verify.yml is the durable fix and is out of scope here only because .github/** is a framework path no plan may change.

The plan is deliberately unverifiable by `yarn test`. If the note is later reworded into two lines, or the author changed to a bot login, nothing in CI will notice — the same advisory gap that produced this ticket.
